axioms.title: A later owner ruling beats an earlier one, wherever it is written
axioms.conflict: Your rule (an open alpha ticket wins) assumes the alpha ticket holds the newer ruling. In these pairs it does not: a newer ruling of yours sits in a later ticket or a completed one.
axioms.draftRuling: When two owner rulings disagree, the later-dated one wins, whatever file holds it; the ticket rule applies only when the dates can't be told apart.

cases.question: How many good deeds open the expedition camp in the alpha: 6, or 10?

a.text: 6 good deeds, as FEAT-103 rules; the run is shorter.

b.text: 10 good deeds, as src/economy.js ships today, so a region-1 run takes about 12 days.
b.quote: maybe 12 days should be expected for a R1 run

cases.why: FEAT-103 is the open alpha ticket, but the 10 came later from the owner's own 12-day remark; it was set as an agent's default, not ruled.

cases.question: When rain lands, does par use that day's grip, or does par stay purely geometric?

a.text: Par uses the day's μ, so a safe driver in the wet can still make rank.

b.text: Par scales with nothing; the wet day is simply harder.

cases.why: SM-INV-2 lists what par must not scale with (the car, run age); weather is the world, not the player, so it may not be the same kind of input.
